title: Introduction to OpenAI Agents SDK
summary: The OpenAI Agents SDK provides a lightweight framework for building AI agents with Python. It simplifies agent creation by offering built-in tools, handoffs, and guardrails. This module covers installation, basic concepts, and your first agent.
key_facts: The SDK requires Python 3.8+ and installs via 'pip install openai-agents'
Agents consist of instructions, tools, and an LLM model

title: Agent Architecture and Components
summary: An agent in the SDK is composed of a name, instructions, model, tools, and optional handoffs. The instructions define the agent's behavior and personality. Tools extend the agent's capabilities beyond text generation.
key_facts: Instructions are the system prompt that guides agent behavior
Tools are Python functions decorated with @function_tool

title: Creating and Running Your First Agent
summary: Creating an agent involves instantiating the Agent class with required parameters. The Runner class executes agents asynchronously with user input. Results include the final output and any tool calls made.
key_facts: Use Runner.run(agent, input) for single-turn or Runner.run_sync for synchronous execution
The result object contains final_output, new_items, and usage metadata

title: Function Tools and Tool Calling
summary: Function tools allow agents to execute Python code during conversations. Decorate functions with @function_tool to register them. The SDK automatically generates JSON schemas from type hints for the LLM.
key_facts: Type hints are mandatory for @function_tool to generate proper schemas
Tools can return any JSON-serializable value including dicts and lists

title: Agent Handoffs and Multi-Agent Systems
summary: Handoffs enable agents to delegate tasks to specialized sub-agents. Define handoffs as a list of Agent instances in the parent agent. The SDK handles context transfer automatically during handoff.
key_facts: Handoffs are one-way transfers; the new agent takes over completely
Use Agent.handoffs parameter to register sub-agents

title: Guardrails for Safety and Validation
summary: Guardrails validate agent inputs and outputs before and after LLM calls. Input guardrails check user messages; output guardrails verify agent responses. They can trigger escalation or provide corrective feedback.
key_facts: Guardrails are async functions returning GuardrailFunctionOutput
Tripwires in guardrails can halt execution and transfer to a fallback agent

title: Tracing and Debugging Agent Runs
summary: The SDK integrates with OpenAI's tracing platform for observability. Traces capture every step including tool calls, handoffs, and LLM responses. Enable tracing by setting the OPENAI_API_KEY environment variable.
key_facts: Traces appear in the OpenAI dashboard under the Traces tab
Use RunConfig to customize trace metadata and sampling

title: Streaming Responses and Real-Time Output
summary: Streaming delivers partial responses as they're generated for better UX. Use Runner.run_streamed() to get an async iterator over response events. Events include text deltas, tool calls, and completion signals.
key_facts: Streamed runs return a StreamedRunResult with async event iteration
TextDelta events contain incremental response chunks

title: Session Management and Conversation History
summary: Sessions maintain conversation state across multiple turns. The SDK stores history automatically when using the same session ID. Sessions persist tool results and agent responses for context.
key_facts: Pass session_id to Runner.run() to maintain history
Session data is stored in-memory by default; use custom storage for persistence

title: Structured Output with Pydantic Models
summary: Structured output forces the LLM to return data matching a Pydantic schema. Define output_type on the Agent with a Pydantic model. The SDK validates and parses responses automatically.
key_facts: Set output_type=MyModel on Agent to enforce structured responses
Validation errors trigger automatic retries with corrective feedback

title: Context Management and Dependencies
summary: Context allows passing runtime data like user info, DB connections, or config to tools. Define a context class and pass it to Runner.run(). Tools access context via RunContextWrapper.
key_facts: Context is generic; define a dataclass or Pydantic model for type safety
Access context in tools with ctx.context.field_name

title: Run Configuration and Customization
summary: RunConfig controls execution behavior including model settings, tracing, and guardrails. Customize max_turns, timeout, and metadata per run. RunConfig applies to both sync and streaming runs.
key_facts: max_turns limits total agent-tool iterations to prevent infinite loops
trace_metadata adds custom tags for filtering in the dashboard

title: Error Handling and Resilience Patterns
summary: The SDK raises specific exceptions for different failure modes. Handle ModelBehaviorError for guardrail trips, MaxTurnsExceeded for loops. Implement retry logic and fallback agents for production resilience.
key_facts: Catch AgentsException base class for all SDK errors
Use try/except around Runner.run() for graceful degradation

title: Best Practices and Production Deployment
summary: Production agents need monitoring, evaluation, and versioning. Use tracing for observability, guardrails for safety, and structured output for reliability. Test with diverse inputs and implement gradual rollout.
key_facts: Always set max_turns and timeouts to prevent runaway costs
Version agent instructions and tools alongside your application code
